frequency_question: How often do announced steep unilateral tariffs on major allied trade partners actually take effect on schedule rather than being rescinded, delayed, or replaced by a deal?
membership_rule: Includes explicitly announced numerical tariff rates on specific allied partner imports with a set implementation date; excludes routine antidumping/countervailing duties and broad non-specific statutory investigations.

cases.name: Section 232 Steel and Aluminum Tariffs on Canada and Mexico
Threatened 5% escalating to 25% Tariffs on All Mexican Imports (Immigration leverage)
Section 232 Threat of 25% Tariffs on European Autos

coverage_note: 3 major high-stakes allied tariff threat episodes identified since 2018
known_gaps: Excludes smaller bilateral disputes outside North America and Europe.
skeleton: Threat cycles categorized by whether the target is an integrated supply-chain partner (Canada/Mexico) versus external allies (EU/Asia), noting the higher friction of self-harm in integrated sectors.
multiplier: 1 hit out of 2 relevant integrated North American border threat events (2018 steel/aluminum implemented vs 2019 Mexico immigration tariffs averted)
validity_reason: Valid through the current presidential term as trade negotiation style remains consistent.
